arturo-fuente--fuente-fuente-opusx.description: The first cigar made entirely from Dominican tobacco, rolled in a wrapper the Fuente family grows on its own Chateau de la Fuente farm. Smooth and bold at once, it carries pepper, cedar and leather on the sweet, lingering fullness of that estate-grown leaf.

thirds.notes: Black pepper up front, then cedar, coffee and leather.
The pepper settles as a caramel-like sweetness appears with cocoa, coffee and roasted nuts.
Dark chocolate and espresso deepen toward a long cedar and pepper finish.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Fuente Fuente OpusX
Arturo Fuente – Chateau de la Fuente

arturo-fuente--gran-reserva.description: The flagship series of the Fuente house, rolled by hand in the Dominican Republic from a reserve of vintage Dominican binder and filler, aged in Spanish cedar vaults and offered under Cameroon, Connecticut shade or Ecuadorian sun-grown wrappers. It includes the 8-5-8, a blend first made by Arturo Fuente and named for his age at his death.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Gran Reserva

Cigar Inspector – Arturo Fuente Flor Fina 8-5-8 review

thirds.notes: In the Cameroon-wrapped 8-5-8, cedar and a soft, creamy vanilla sweetness open, with clove-like spice and a little black pepper.
Cedar deepens and earth comes in, while cocoa, almond and a touch of coffee fill out the steady, gentle sweetness.
Leather takes over with cedar and earth, a caramel-like sweetness and a creamier texture toward the close.

arturo-fuente--chateau-fuente-series.description: Sharing its name with Chateau de la Fuente, the family's tobacco farm, this series is hand-rolled in the Dominican Republic from the family's private reserve of aged Dominican filler. It comes in Connecticut shade, broadleaf maduro and Ecuadorian sun-grown wrappers, with the King T presented in a tube that shows the farm.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – cigar catalogue
Holt's – Arturo Fuente Chateau Series
After Action Cigars – Arturo Fuente Chateau Natural review

thirds.notes: In the Connecticut-wrapped Rothschild, rounded cedar leads over a buttery, bready note and nuts, with a hint of white pepper through the nose.
Creaminess grows, the nuttiness folds into the blend and light leather appears, with sweet cedar and a quiet spice behind.
Cedar turns to toasted wood, the nuts lean toward roasted almond and a light earthiness settles in; it stays cool and gentle to the end.

arturo-fuente--hemingway.description: Introduced in 1983 when shaped cigars had all but vanished, the Hemingway revived the perfecto, a figurado that is among the hardest shapes to roll. A Cameroon wrapper covers Dominican binder and filler, giving a medium smoke of cedar, cream and gentle sweetness with soft baking spice, well suited to a short break.

thirds.notes: Cedar and cream with a little coffee, a brown-sugar sweetness and light Cameroon spice.
Toasted wood and cedar lead, the sweetness turns toward honey and baking spice grows clearer.
Drier and spicier, with white pepper sharpening and a light cocoa note at the end.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – cigar catalogue
Arturo Fuente – The Fuente Family (media kit)
After Action Cigars – Hemingway Best Seller review
halfwheel – Hemingway Short Story review
Kaplowitz – Hemingway Short Story review

arturo-fuente--hemingway-maduro.description: The Hemingway perfecto shapes in a Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper over Dominican binder and filler, made in limited quantities. Heartier than the Cameroon original, it pairs dark chocolate and creamy coffee with cinnamon-like spice, and turns to cedar and a little pepper toward the end, an after-dinner choice.

thirds.notes: Dark chocolate and creamy coffee with cinnamon-like spice and a soft leathery retrohale.
Spice grows while richer, earthy chocolate and cedar build, with a hint of raisin.
Charred oak and chocolate lead, with a leathery, peppery finish and some creaminess returning.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – cigar catalogue
The Cigar Authority – Hemingway Classic Maduro review
Stogie Review – Hemingway Masterpiece Maduro

arturo-fuente--don-carlos.description: Launched in 1986 and named for Carlos Fuente Sr., this blend wraps vintage Dominican tobaccos, some aged up to ten years, in a Cameroon leaf. It smokes with cedar, leather and earth, gathering cocoa and a soft sweetness of dark fruit and vanilla as it goes, a refined cigar for a quiet hour.

thirds.notes: Cedar and oak-like wood with lightly roasted coffee, leather and a faint pepper.
Leather takes the lead; cocoa sweetness, cinnamon-like spice and a hint of honey develop.
Earth comes forward with dark fruit, vanilla and a creamy coffee finish, ending smooth.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Don Carlos
Arturo Fuente – The Fuente Family (media kit)
Bourbon & Banter – Don Carlos Robusto review
The Cigar Authority – Don Carlos Double Robusto review

arturo-fuente--don-carlos-edicion-de-ani.description: An anniversary edition of the Don Carlos, the line named for Carlos Fuente Sr., made by Tabacalera A. Fuente in the Dominican Republic. Instead of the usual Cameroon leaf it carries a shade-grown Dominican wrapper, and it is listed as medium in strength, in robusto, double robusto and toro sizes.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Don Carlos
Holt's – Don Carlos Edicion de Aniversario

arturo-fuente--anejo.description: Born after Hurricane Georges ruined the OpusX wrapper crop in 1998, the Añejo uses a related blend of Dominican binder and filler under a Connecticut broadleaf maduro wrapper aged for years, partly in Cognac barrels. Released only a few times a year, it smokes rich and dark with brown sugar, oak, coffee and pepper.

thirds.notes: Brown-sugar sweetness with oak, cedar, cinnamon and black pepper on the retrohale.
The sweetness deepens, then gives way to dark coffee and earth, with cocoa and strong pepper.
Rich and chewy: black coffee and earth lead, cinnamon returns and a faint sweetness lingers.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Añejo
Arturo Fuente – cigar catalogue
The Cigar Authority – Añejo No. 50 review
Smoke Into Oblivion – Añejo No. 50 review

arturo-fuente--especiales.description: A small Arturo Fuente line made in the Dominican Republic under an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper, offered in three sizes: Cazadores, Conquistadores and Emperador. It is listed as mild to medium in strength, which places it among the gentler cigars in the Fuente range.

sources.title: Holt's – Arturo Fuente Especiales
Holt's Clubhouse – Arturo Fuente Especiales Conquistadores review

thirds.notes: Cedar, leather and cinnamon open with cocoa nib and a brief caramel-cream sweetness, and almost no pepper.
The profile holds steady as the draw opens up, and the strength builds slightly around the midpoint.
Toward the last inches the strength settles at a firm medium, with a clean, lingering finish.

arturo-fuente--seleccion-d-oro.description: A Gran Reserva variant from Tabacalera A. Fuente in the Dominican Republic, finished in a Connecticut shade wrapper and offered only in the longer Corona Imperial, Seleccion Privada No. 1 and Churchill sizes. It is listed as medium in strength, a lighter-coloured take on the house's classic shapes.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Gran Reserva
Holt's – Arturo Fuente Seleccion d'Oro

arturo-fuente--claro.description: Classic Arturo Fuente shapes such as the 8-5-8, Curly Head, Spanish Lonsdale, Privada No. 1 and Churchill, made in the Dominican Republic and finished in a green candela wrapper. The quickly cured leaf keeps its colour and gives a lighter style, listed as medium in strength.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Gran Reserva
Holt's – Arturo Fuente Claro

arturo-fuente--rare-pink.description: A Fuente line in Hemingway-style shapes such as Short Story, Signature and Work of Art, alongside sizes like Queen of Hearts, made in the Dominican Republic under an Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper. The reddish rosado leaf sets it apart within the range, and it is listed as medium in strength.

sources.title: Holt's – Arturo Fuente Rare Pink

arturo-fuente--it-s-a-boy-it-s-a-girl.description: A limited Brevas Royale from Arturo Fuente, banded either It's a Boy or It's a Girl for celebrating a birth. Made in the Dominican Republic with a Connecticut shade wrapper, it is listed as medium in strength, an approachable cigar to share with guests at a family occasion.

sources.title: Holt's – Arturo Fuente It's a Boy / It's a Girl

arturo-fuente--casa-cuba.description: The last blend created by Carlos Fuente Sr., revived from an old family brand for the 2013 celebrations, with Cuban-seed Dominican binder and long filler under an Ecuadorian Havana wrapper. He blended it the way he once worked with Cuban tobacco, and each size is named after a domino, such as the Doble Cinco robusto.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Casa Cuba
Arturo Fuente – Casa Cuba, a Carlos Fuente Sr. original
Arturo Fuente – The Fuente Family (media kit)

arturo-fuente--opusx-oro-oscuro.description: An OpusX variant in which the Dominican wrapper from the Fuente estate is given extra ageing and fermentation, set over select Dominican binder and filler. The longer cure darkens the leaf and gives a deeper, more robust finish than the standard OpusX, in sizes from the Robusto to the Reserva D'Chateau.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – cigar catalogue

arturo-fuente--opusx-angel-s-share.description: Created after a 2012 fire destroyed tobacco the Fuente family had been ageing since the late 1940s, this OpusX uses a wrapper from the middle primings, lighter and sweeter than the usual top leaves. Its name borrows the winemaker's term for what evaporates from the barrel, and part of its sales supports the Cigar Family Charitable Foundation.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Angel's Share
Arturo Fuente – The Fuente Family (media kit)

JR Cigars Blending Room – Arturo Fuente Opus X Angel's Share

thirds.notes: Sweet, faintly smoky tobacco and fruit sit over black pepper, earth and cream, with hay and aged wood arriving as it settles.
The smoky sweetness moves to the front and the pepper grows, alternating red and black, with earth and hay beneath.
Pepper becomes the main supporting note and the wood grows more evident, while fruit, earth and cream round it off.

arturo-fuente--opusx-the-lost-city.description: A limited release in the OpusX family from Tabacalera A. Fuente in the Dominican Republic, finished like the core OpusX in a Dominican wrapper. It is listed as full in strength and comes in robusto, double robusto, toro, lancero and piramide sizes, with a tubed double robusto.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – The Fuente Family (media kit)

Smoke Inn – Arturo Fuente OpusX Lost City Double Robusto review
Cigar Obsession – Fuente Fuente OpusX Lost City Robusto review
Regency Cigar – OpusX Lost City review

thirds.notes: A first burst of pepper soon softens into leather, earth and cinnamon spice over natural sweetness, with cedar and oak in the background.
Pepper recedes as cocoa joins the leather and earth, with dried fruit, a light nuttiness and oak adding depth.
The notes merge into cocoa, spice and mild sweetness, with a bitter touch of espresso and oak to finish.

arturo-fuente--forbidden-x.description: Presented by the Fuente family as an evolution of the OpusX, Forbidden X draws on the rarest tobacco selections from Chateau de la Fuente. Carlito ages the blend in barrels kept in a closed area of the factory, and the four sizes, from Deseos D'Amor to Amor Sensual, come twenty to a box.

sources.title: Arturo Fuente – Forbidden X

arturo-fuente--opusx-20th-anniversary.description: A limited OpusX edition marking twenty years of the first all-Dominican cigar, made by Tabacalera A. Fuente. Carlos Fuente Jr. conceived it as a tribute to his family and his childhood, and the four sizes carry the names Believe, Father & Son, Power of the Dream and God's Whisper, twenty cigars to a box.
